goal: Create a weekly team-update skill from supplied project notes

sources.title: GitLab Communication handbook
sources.notes: Read the asynchronous communication, internal communication, and issue cross-linking guidance. It supports giving readers explicit context and meaningful link descriptions; our defaults remain design inferences, not demonstrated performance results.

questions.title: Who needs to understand the update without attending the project meetings?
questions.help: The audience changes how much context belongs beside each change.
questions.decision: How much shared project knowledge the generated skill may assume

options.label: The immediate project team
options.effect: Keep context short when the notes establish shared terminology

options.label: Teammates and cross-functional partners
options.effect: Explain unfamiliar project terms and connect changes with their supported consequence

recommendation.rationale: The example is intended to remain useful to people outside the project meetings.
assumptions: Recipients are authorized to read the supplied material

questions.title: Where should supplied evidence links appear?
questions.decision: How readers trace claims back to their supplied sources

options.label: Beside the relevant claim
options.effect: Place descriptive source links next to the claims they support

options.label: In a short source list after the update
options.effect: Group source links after the prose while keeping each claim-to-source relationship identifiable

recommendation.rationale: Readers can check a significant statement without searching a separate list.
assumptions: The notes contain shareable source links when links are needed

questions.title: What should happen when the notes leave a material gap?
questions.help: A missing owner, unconfirmed date, or conflicting release status can change the meaning of the update.
questions.decision: Whether unresolved information delays drafting or stays visible in a useful draft

options.label: Draft now and mark what is uncertain
options.effect: Produce a draft with explicit gaps and focused follow-up where needed

options.label: Resolve material gaps before the final draft
options.effect: Ask for the defined missing facts before producing the final draft

recommendation.rationale: A reviewable draft remains useful when uncertainty is visible and no commitments are invented.
assumptions: The draft is reviewed before external publication

questions.title: Which missing facts must be resolved before drafting?
questions.help: This is only needed for the clarification-first workflow.
questions.decision: Which gaps block the final draft rather than remain explicitly uncertain

recommendation.value: Resolve contradictory release status, unconfirmed commitments, and unclear ownership of an urgent request.
recommendation.rationale: These details can change what the update asks someone to believe or do.
assumptions: Minor wording gaps do not block drafting
